passage:
The light in one school hallway stayed on all night. A student noticed it when he passed the school after dinner.
The next day, he told the science teacher. The teacher helped him calculate how much electricity one light could use in a month.
The number was not huge, but it was not nothing. The student council then checked other lights, fans, and projectors around school.
They made reminder stickers: "Last out Lights out."
Within two months, the school used less electricity.
The project began with one hallway light. It showed that saving energy is not only about large machines or big plans. It can begin when someone notices a small waste and says something.
